Hannah —

Thanks for sending over the template. We attached our redline and an SCCs table with a few carveouts and a proposed amendment to retention. High-level asks from our side: 1) We need the DPA to reflect a 24-month retention cap for customer data and backups (our compliance board requires this), 2) carve out aggregate analytics data from the retention calc, 3) confirm cross-border transfers via SCCs are acceptable and provide a final SCC attachment, and 4) we need a contact for the DPIA evidence (if you have a template).

We also have a short list of questions on subprocessors in the redline (section 4.3) — can you confirm available subprocessor roster and a timing commitment for updates?

Subject: Re: RetailStream DPA redline and SCC questions

Sam —

Appreciate the clear redline. High-level response below and next steps:

1) Retention cap: Our standard is 36 months, but we can agree to a 24-month cap for data subject to the agreement provided we add a limited exception for short-term backups (up to 90 days) to ensure incident recovery. Marissa (legal ops) is on this thread to confirm final language.

2) Aggregate analytics: We can carve out anonymized/aggregated analytics from retention obligations provided the data is irreversibly aggregated and cannot be re-identified. Please confirm the fields you intend to aggregate so we can align on a definition.

3) SCCs & transfers: We are comfortable using the EU Commission SCCs as an attachment. Dev can confirm which SCC module maps to our hosting configuration. We'll provide a completed SCCs Attachment and a short importer note for your DPO.

4) DPIA evidence: We do not share customer DPIAs, but we can provide a DPIA checklist and a summary of processing that should assist your DPO. If RetailStream requires a joint-DPIA session, we can schedule one with our Privacy Lead.

Subprocessors: we can provide a current roster and a 30-day notice commitment for additions. We cannot commit to a longer retention of subprocessor lists than our public roster cadence, but we will put a 30-day SLA in writing in the DPA.

Next steps proposed:
- Marissa to propose redline compromises on retention + backup exception (target: today EOD).
- Dev to produce SCCs attachment and subprocessor roster (target: tomorrow).
- I will prepare a signing sequence and DocuSign envelope with exec-level signers mapped.

If you'd like to review on a call, let us know availability — Hannah

Hannah Schmitt

Samuel / team —

Quick follow-up from Legal Ops after reviewing the redline. Proposed language (summary):
- Retention: Accept 24 months for customer account data; add a narrowly scoped backup exception allowing restoration copies retained no longer than 90 days from creation. We will add a clause that production backups are encrypted and rotated per our standard key lifecycle policy.
- Analytics carveout: We will accept carveout for data that meets our irreversible aggregation definition. Please confirm sample schema.
- SCCs: We will attach the EU SCCs and include a cover page stating our technical and organizational measures (high level). Dev — please attach the SCC module mapping and hosting region note as a separate file for their DPO.
- Subprocessor updates: Commit to 30 days notice for new subprocessors and provide an up-to-date roster as an attachment to the DPA.

I am attaching a short comment file with line edits (I will upload to the Drive after this thread). If RetailStream agrees, we can finalize edits and I will prepare the DocuSign envelope. Proposed signer map: RetailStream exec (CEO or General Counsel) + Redwood exec (VP Revenue) for signatures; Legal Ops will countersign internally and retain execution evidence.

Attachments to follow: consolidated_redline_comment_view.docx
